content:
olivia: Heads up — eu-west-1 GPU pools showing a capacity skew. AZ-1 has ~6/8 GPUs idle, AZ-2 is starved and we have ~120 pending model-serving pods. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

sam: Yep, noticed pending spike at 09:04 UTC. Scheduler logs show repeated predicate failures: "InsufficientGPU" and backpressure on the scheduling queue.

raj: Could be taints/affinity mismatch after the last infra rollout. Did we change tolerations for the dedicated pools?

kevin: I pulled a describe on a pending pod: 
```
kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -n models
kubectl describe pod model-x-56 -n models
```
Describe shows a required nodeAffinity for gpu.family=rtx6000 and a toleration for key=dedicated,value=inference,effect=NoSchedule.

infra-bot: autoscaler-event: scaleUp attempted for group gpu-eu-west-2 at 2026-03-18T09:07Z — desired capacity delta 0->2 (failed due to AZ capacity limits)

olivia: The weird part: AZ-1 nodes are smaller spot instances and currently underutilized. AZ-2 has reserved p4s. Scheduler is preferring AZ-2 because the tolerations + hard topology spread we added force even distribution, but nodeAffinity weight and our reserved instance labels make AZ-2 the only match. So pods pend instead of filling AZ-1.

sam: Can you paste the actual podSpec (affinity/tolerations/topologySpread)?

olivia: snippet:
```
nodeAffinity:
  requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
    nodeSelectorTerms:
    - matchExpressions:
      - key: gpu.family
        operator: In
        values: ["rtx6000"]
tolerations:
- key: "dedicated"
  operator: "Equal"
  value: "inference"
  effect: "NoSchedule"
priorityClassName: "high-throughput"
topologySpreadConstraints:
- maxSkew: 1
  topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
  whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
  labelSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: model-serving
```

raj: That topologySpread is too strict (maxSkew:1 + DoNotSchedule). Combined with required nodeAffinity this can block placement when instance types differ across AZs. Also priorityClass + no preemption = pending forever.

kevin: Short mitigation options: 1) convert spread constraint to "WhenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway" or increase maxSkew to 2; 2) add a preferred (soft) nodeAffinity term for AZ-1 so scheduler can place there; 3) temporarily lower priority for non-critical replicas to allow preemption. Which do we want to try first?

olivia: Proposed plan: 1) Patch the deployment to change topologySpreadConstraints to maxSkew:2 and whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway (prefer), 2) add a soft nodeAffinity term with weight 1 for nodes labeled zone=eu-west-1a (AZ-1), 3) scale up spot pool in AZ-1 by +2 to absorb immediate load, 4) run a targeted cordon/drain on two stale AZ-2 nodes to force rebalance during low traffic window (11:00 UTC). I'll open a ticket and coordinate. :thumbsup:

sam: +1. Please include exact kubectl patch commands and rollback steps in the runbook. Note cost tradeoff: shifting from reserved p4s to more spot rtx instances could save ~35-45% but might raise eviction risk. Capture that delta.

raj: I'll prepare a small scheduler-policy PR to relax required nodeAffinity for autoscaled inference pools (turn required->preferred with weight adjustment) so this doesn't recur after autoscaler events.

infra-bot: ticket CREATED: INFRA-4821 "eu-west-1 AZ skew + topology constraints" assigned to olivia, raj

kevin: After changes monitor eviction rate, pending pod count, and model latency SLOs. If SLOs degrade or cost spikes unexpectedly, be ready to rollback.

olivia: Will execute changes at 11:00 UTC and post updates here. Runbook draft (will attach to ticket): 
- kubectl patch deployment model-serving -n models --type json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/topologySpreadConstraints/0/maxSkew","value":2},{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/topologySpreadConstraints/0/whenUnsatisfiable","value":"ScheduleAnyway"}]'
- apply preferred affinity patch:
```
kubectl patch deployment model-serving -n models --type=json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/affinity/nodeAffinity/preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution","value":[{"weight":1,"preference":{"matchExpressions":[{"key":"topology.kubernetes.io/zone","operator":"In","values":["eu-west-1a"]}]}}]}]'
```
- scale spot nodegroup: aws cli command in ticket.

sam: Thanks. Also add metric queries for pending pods by zone and a dashboard alert for skew > 50% for > 5m.

kevin: Sounds good. Keep ops on call in case of regressions. :rocket:

olivia: I'll update after the window. Thanks everyone!
